text:
Anya: FYI ran the adjudicator suite with the new 8-bit quantized candidate and saw a weird shift in tie rates vs the float baseline. overall win-rate looks fine but ties doubled.
Matt: hmm interesting — do you mean literal identical scores or close/confidence ties?
Anya: literal identical label from the judge on >10% of evaluation pairs where baseline chose A or B. not rounding issue AFAICT.
Sam: could be a runner bug that buckets low-confidence outputs as 'uncertain' then maps to tied. saw something similar with the batch shuffler last month.
June: can you paste the failing snippet / command you ran?
Anya: Sure:```bash
./eval-runner --suite=adjudicators --model candidate-q8 --baseline=adjudicator-v2 --pairs=5000 --seed=42 --threads=8
```
Anya: And the tail of the log:```
WARNING: kv-cache empty for 0.0s, treating as cold start
ERROR: adjudicator_runner.process_pair: unknown decision bucket 'tie_confidence'
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "runner/main.py", line 423, in process_batch
    result = adjudicate(pair)
  File "runner/adjudicator.py", line 88, in adjudicate
    return map_bucket(decision)
KeyError: 'tie_confidence'
```
Priya: That KeyError suggests the new judge returned a decision label that the runner mapping doesn't know about. we recently added 'ambiguous' label in the schema but forgot to push runner mappings.
Matt: yep — schema drift. eval-bot schema check should have caught this in CI. why didn't it? :thinking:
eval-bot: automated message: adjudicator schema v2.3 has new label variants: ['ambiguous', 'low_confidence', 'tie_confidence']. CI rule 'adjudicator-label-check' did not run for this branch.
June: CI wiring flake then. we've seen intermittent skips when runner tests time out. I'll open a ticket.
Sam: aside from the bug, the doubling of ties worries me. quantized models can be less calibrated. if calibration dips, tie thresholds that worked for float might be inappropriate.
Anya: good point. current tie rule is simple: if top_score - runner_score < 0.02 -> tie. we tuned that on float models.
Priya: propose we add two things: 1) calibration check per-judge (ECE over a calibration probe set) 2) a weighted tie-breaker that uses judge calibration to bias toward more confident judges.
Matt: concretely, we could compute calibrated_score = raw_score * (1 - ECE) and then compare margins. or use Platt scaling on logits.
June: both okay. Platt scaling requires a held-out calibration fold. do we have one for adjudicators?
Anya: we do — eval/bench/adjudicator_calibration.jsonl with ~3k examples across genres.
Sam: also add a meta-metric: pairwise_agreement (PA) and consensus_entropy (CE). PA = fraction of pairs where majority exists. CE = average entropy of the decision distribution across judges. this flags judges that cause instability.
Priya: for tie-breaker policy, options: majority, weighted-by-calibration, human-in-loop-for-ambiguous. which should be default?
Matt: default to weighted-by-calibration with fallback to majority. human only when CE > threshold (e.g., >0.9). keep human fallbacks as a sampling policy rather than blocking.
Anya: I want to be careful about demographic bias. earlier we saw the baseline adjudicator favored one phrasing in a sensitive dataset. quantization shouldn't amplify that, but we need subgroup agreement checks.
June: add subgroup disagreement reports to the dashboard. subgroup PA and subgroup CE. associate with metadata tags in the evaluation examples.
Sam: action items: 1) fix runner mapping to accept new labels (hotfix) 2) update CI rule to enforce label-check (June) 3) add calibration probe and ECE calc to adjudicator pipeline (Anya/Priya) 4) implement weighted tie-breaker and metrics (Matt/Sam) 5) dashboard tiles for subgroup PA/CE (June)
Priya: I'll draft a PR with the schema mapping and unit tests for unknown label handling. target: today.
Anya: I'll run the calibration scripts on candidate-q8 and post ECE numbers in this thread.
Matt: I'll prototype the weighted tie-breaker and run ablation (float vs q8) on 1k pairs first.
June: filing ticket ENGML-872: "adjudicator labels CI + tie-breaker metrics and dashboard" with the action items. linking to doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/evals/adjudicator-rubric-guidelines (please add notes) :eyes:
Sam: tiny nit — update our eval docs to avoid using 'tie' as a single bucket name. prefer 'ambiguous_for_majority' or 'no_majority'. helps clarity.
Anya: agreed. I'll rename local outputs and add a converter script for old artifacts.
Priya: any objections to running the full 5k pairs after the runner mapping fix?
Matt: go for it once the mapping and CI are fixed. schedule it overnight.
Anya: thanks everyone. will post results and ECE numbers when done. :thumbsup:
